releases.notes:
## Fixed
- The rider HUD now shows the cooling rate with at most two decimals (for example 0.33/s).
- Fireballs now launch from the Happy Ghast’s mouth instead of beside the pilot’s head.

For Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer, Fabric API 0.160.7+26.3, and Java 25 or newer.

Install on the server, or in your Fabric installation for single-player. Multiplayer clients do not need the mod.

releases.notes:
# Happy Artillery 1.2.1

Happy Artillery now supports Minecraft 26.3. This release keeps the same artillery, controls, heat, Cry, overheat, and rider HUD behavior from 1.2.0 while updating the server mod for Minecraft 26.3.

- Added support for Minecraft 26.3.
- Updated the requirement to Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer and Fabric API 0.160.7+26.3.
- Prevented generated controls from being stored in bundles while using Creative mode.

This release is for **Minecraft 26.3** and **Java 25 or newer**. Use Happy Artillery 1.2.0 for Minecraft 26.2. Happy Artillery remains server-side; players can join with an unmodded Java client.

releases.notes:
# Happy Artillery 1.2.0

Fire from the hotbar slots you choose, hold to keep shooting, and watch your ghast's cooling rate between bursts. Ammo is gone: cooldowns, heat, and overheat now govern how long you can keep firing.

## Controls and firing

- Fire and Cry now use temporary controls you can move around your hotbar, main inventory, and offhand. They no longer take over fixed slots or alter your existing items.
- Controls are given only to the pilot. With both abilities enabled, you need two free hotbar or main-inventory slots; if there isn't enough room, nothing is overwritten.
- Hold Fire Control to keep shooting. Cry remains a separate click-to-use sound with its own cooldown.
- Vanilla ghast fireballs now launch clear of the ghast and its passengers.
- Aiming Fire Control at a nearby block starts firing without setting that block alight through the control item's vanilla use.
- Controls can't be turned into crafting ingredients, stored in bundles, loaded as ammunition, or used as their underlying vanilla item. Dropping one or moving it into a container, crafting grid, or armor slot consumes it. Dismount and ride again to replace a missing control.

## Heat and rider feedback

- The rider display shows firing status and the actual cooling rate, including when there's no cooling. Passengers can follow the same heat status without gaining firing controls.
- The heat bar uses your Happy Ghast's name. Pilots also get a warning when a control is missing or tucked away in the main inventory.
- Heat, ability cooldowns, and pending overheat fuses survive chunk unloads and server restarts. Changing riders doesn't reset the ghast's cooldowns, and dismounting doesn't cancel a pending detonation.
- Fresh configurations use retuned heat, cooling, explosion, and Cry settings. Existing settings with direct equivalents are preserved during migration rather than replaced by the new defaults.
- Removed ammunition and passive ammunition refill.
- Removed water cooling. Touching water blocks firing by default and always blocks Cry.

Cold areas still cool faster, hot areas cool more slowly, and the Nether has no passive cooling by default. **Overheating destroys the Happy Ghast by default**, with an explosion and a burst of fireballs.

## For server owners

- Added `/ha reload` for permission level 2 admins. Invalid changes report the problem and leave the previous working settings active.
- Configuration is grouped by feature, and you can supply just the settings you want to change. Valid files keep their contents during startup and reload.
- Released 1.1.x configs migrate with an exact backup saved as `happy-artillery.json.v1.1.2.bak`. Customized removed settings or incompatible biome heat limits stop migration with an error instead of silently losing your choices. Read the [upgrade notes](https://github.com/ff-tech-xyz/happy-artillery/blob/main/README.md#upgrading-from-11x).
- Firing speed, cooling-display colors, and heat warnings are configurable. See the [configuration reference](https://github.com/ff-tech-xyz/happy-artillery/blob/main/docs/happy-artillery-config.jsonc).
- The central overheat explosion and direct fire placement now respect `mobGriefing` when `overheat.breaksBlocks` is enabled. Disabling that setting stops those terrain effects, **not the normal impact effects of emitted vanilla fireballs**.

This release is for **Minecraft 26.2**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.3+**, **Fabric API**, and **Java 25+**. Happy Artillery remains server-side; players can use unmodded Java clients. The project is now licensed under **CC0 1.0 Universal**.
